truth.description: 去掉了结尾锚点 $，"123456.1234" 这类小数位过多的时间戳也会被当成 ATT 句子匹配。

findings.message: No test was added for the exact regression described in the issue. The patch only touches pynmea2/types/proprietary/ash.py; test_ash.py's test_ashratt still uses a 3-decimal timestamp ('130533.620'), which matched under the old regex too. The reported failing input ('$PASHR,122144.75,240.68,T,,,,,,,2*04') is not covered anywhere in the test suite, so a future revert of this regex would not be caught.
findings.suggestion: Add a test (e.g. test_ashratt_2dp) that parses a 2-decimal timestamp sentence such as '$PASHR,122144.75,240.68,T,,,,,,,2*04', asserts type(msg) == pynmea2.ash.ASHRATT and msg.timestamp == datetime.time(12, 21, 44, 750000), ideally also asserting render() round-trips.

findings.message: The issue explicitly recommended '^\d{6}\.\d{2,3}$', but the patch dropped the trailing '$' anchor: '^\d{6}\.\d{2,3}'. The unanchored pattern also matches fields that merely *begin* with such a value (e.g. '122144.75123' or '122144.75X'). ASHRATT.match is only consulted as the fallback for unregistered ASH subtypes (ash.py:23-26), so any unregistered message whose 2nd field starts like a 6-digit time with 2-3 decimals will now be classified as ASHRATT rather than the generic ASH.
findings.suggestion: Restore the end anchor as suggested in the issue: r'^\d{6}\.\d{2,3}$'. If broader fraction lengths should also be accepted (the input must be a valid hhmmss[.ss...] timestamp), use r'^\d{6}\.\d+$' instead — but keep the '$' so partial-prefix matches don't cause misclassification.
